scope_gaps.note: preprint status and review status are not stated in the snapshot; only an arXiv submission with no venue is shown.

Direction of injection (into responses) is not stated in the abstract. The source says touching researcher-owned canary credentials (AWS credentials, plus an ETH private key); the Polish says dostęp do kluczy, a looser wording. Findings are counts in a purchased and collected sample, not rates for the market.
Plaintext access is described for the class of routers, not measured per router; the payload covers more than requests.
The study did not test price as a predictor of safety. It shows only that 1 of the paid routers injected malicious code; in the abstract's counts the paid and free groups both contain such routers.
The paper is more than a measurement study (poisoning studies, a research proxy, defense evaluation).
The abstract does not discuss representativeness either way; the sample came from Taobao, Xianyu, Shopify-hosted storefronts and public communities.
Authorisation, confidentiality assessment and the legal basis for processing are legal and organisational matters outside the source (Polish and EU law not covered by any cited snapshot).
The source evaluates automated client-side defenses; no result for them and nothing on permission breadth appears in the abstract.
The source concerns third-party routers, not direct connections to official providers.
The source does not concern personal data or masking at all.
The source does not describe human review of commands.
